name: manual_f0c0ee
claim: A gate copied from a one-time bootstrap path onto a reconcile-on-every-start path must compare identity, not lifecycle state: state legitimately mutates between starts, so a 'must equal the pristine record' check passes first boot and then refuses every restart after the first write. Before accepting a reviewer-proposed hardening, apply it and run the existing restart tests; and reject guards whose conditions the SELECT or a DB constraint already guarantee, which are false assurance.

decisions.notes: phylax PR#11 2026-10-13: two independent reviewers (Codex, AntiGravity) both asked ensure_active_key to require the stored key to equal a pristine record, copying PR#10's register_initial_key gate. record_grant legitimately sets latest_live_expiry on the ACTIVE key and ensure_active_key runs on every start, so applying the gate experimentally failed test_durable_grant_state_survives_authority_restart and test_state_survives_reopening_including_revocation ('provisioned issuer key does not match the durable active key'). AntiGravity's substitute added status!='active', retired_at, retain_until checks that are tautologies under WHERE status='active' and the one_active_issuer_key partial unique index. Consensus between reviewers is not evidence; the empirical run was. The contract is now in the docstring and pinned by a test.
